speaker: Unknown
en: Are you passionate about software development and the tech industry?
zh: 你对软件开发和科技行业充满热情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Software Engineering Daily is looking for a new podcast host to grow its hosting team.
zh: Software Engineering Daily 正在寻找一位新的播客主持人来扩充其主持团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this role, you'll help shape the show's editorial direction and interview engineers, founders, hackers, and tech leaders.
zh: 在这个职位上，你将帮助塑造节目的编辑方向，并采访工程师、创始人、黑客和技术领袖。

speaker: Unknown
en: Podcasting experience is a plus, but not required.
zh: 有播客经验是加分项，但不是必需的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Curiosity, great communication skills, and a genuine interest in the craft of building software are what matter most.
zh: 最重要的是好奇心、出色的沟通能力，以及对构建软件这门手艺的真正兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: If this sounds like you, reach out at editor at softwareengineeringdaily.com.
zh: 如果这听起来像你，请发邮件到 editor at softwareengineeringdaily.com 联系我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Automated browser testing is a foundational technology that many web developers rely on.
zh: 自动化浏览器测试是许多网页开发者所依赖的基础技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Modern tooling lets a single test drive Chrome, Firefox, and Safari the same way, a triumph of software engineering built on years of standardization work.
zh: 现代工具让单个测试可以用同样的方式驱动 Chrome、Firefox 和 Safari，这是建立在多年标准化工作之上的软件工程成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: That standardization emerged from the interplay between open source projects, browser vendors, and standards bodies like the W3C.
zh: 这种标准化源自开源项目、浏览器厂商以及像 W3C 这样的标准机构之间的相互作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: David Burns is a longtime Selenium and WebDriver contributor, a veteran of Mozilla, and is currently the head of developer advocacy and open source at BrowserStack.
zh: David Burns 是 Selenium 和 WebDriver 的长期贡献者，Mozilla 的资深人士，目前是 BrowserStack 的开发者布道与开源负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, David joins Josh Goldberg to discuss how open source projects, browser vendors, and standards bodies fit together, a practical philosophy of testing built around one solid test per critical path, and the risks that AI and vibe coding introduce to web development.
zh: 在本期节目中，David 与 Josh Goldberg 一起讨论开源项目、浏览器厂商和标准机构是如何相互配合的、围绕每条关键路径一个扎实测试而建立的实际测试哲学，以及 AI 和 vibe coding 给网页开发带来的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is hosted by Josh Goldberg, front-end developer at Sentry and open-source maintainer.
zh: 本期节目由 Josh Goldberg 主持，他是 Sentry 的前端开发者和开源维护者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Josh works on projects in the TypeScript ecosystem, most notably TypeScript ESLint, a powerful static analysis toolset for JavaScript and TypeScript.
zh: Josh 从事 TypeScript 生态系统的项目工作，最著名的是 TypeScript ESLint，一个面向 JavaScript 和 TypeScript 的强大静态分析工具集。

speaker: Unknown
en: Josh is also the author of the O'Reilly Learning TypeScript book, a Microsoft MVP for developer technologies, and a co-founder of SquiggleConf, a conference for excellent web developer tooling.
zh: Josh 也是 O'Reilly《Learning TypeScript》一书的作者、微软开发者技术方向的 MVP，以及 SquiggleConf 的联合创始人，这是一个聚焦优秀网页开发者工具的会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Find Josh on Blue Sky, Fostadon, and .com as Joshua K. Goldberg.
zh: 你可以在 Blue Sky、Fostadon 和 .com 上找到 Josh，用户名是 Joshua K. Goldberg。

speaker: Unknown
en: WITH ME TODAY IS DAVID BURNS, HEAD OF DEVELOPER ADVOCACY AND OPENSOURCE AT BROWSER STACK.
zh: 今天和我在一起的是 DAVID BURNS，BROWSER STACK 的开发者布道与开源负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: DAVID, WELCOME TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING DAILY.
zh: DAVID，欢迎来到 SOFTWARE ENGINEERING DAILY。

speaker: Unknown
en: DAVID BURNS, DEVELOPER ADVOCACY AND OPENSOURCE AT BROWSER STACK.
zh: DAVID BURNS，BROWSER STACK 的开发者布道与开源负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: DAVID, WELCOME TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING DAILY.
zh: DAVID，欢迎来到 SOFTWARE ENGINEERING DAILY。

speaker: Unknown
en: DAVID BURNS, Thanks for having me, Josh.
zh: DAVID BURNS：谢谢你邀请我，Josh。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited to be here.
zh: 我真的很高兴能来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: DAVID BURNS, Yeah, we're excited to talk with you.
zh: DAVID BURNS：是啊，我们很高兴和你交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got a lot of cool stuff to talk about, developer advocacy and Selenium and W3C and open source.
zh: 你有很多很酷的东西可以聊，开发者布道、Selenium、W3C 和开源。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before we get into all of that, tell us, how did you get into tech?
zh: 但在深入这些话题之前，跟我们讲讲，你是怎么进入科技行业的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was born and raised in South Africa.
zh: 我出生并成长于南非。

speaker: Unknown
en: I went to university there.
zh: 我在那里上的大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then when I was at university, I was studying computer science and industrial psychology, which I know is kind of slightly weird and wonderful.
zh: 上大学时，我学的是计算机科学和工业心理学，我知道这有点奇怪又奇妙。

speaker: Unknown
en: But my idea then is because I couldn't make up my mind if I wanted to be in tech or a psychologist.
zh: 但我当时是想，因为我无法下定决心是想进入科技行业还是当心理学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then moved to the UK to kind of just do a bit of traveling.
zh: 然后我搬到了英国，打算去旅行一番。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got a really cool job at a bank.
zh: 在一家银行得到了一份很酷的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which was doing kind of process re-engineering.
zh: 那份工作做的是流程再造之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I was like, oh, this is kind of cool.
zh: 然后我就想，哦，这还挺酷的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learned a bit about like process automation and then started at a startup in Southampton, which is on the South coast.
zh: 学了一点流程自动化之类的东西，然后在南安普敦的一家初创公司开始了工作，南安普敦在南部海岸。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was their QA hire.
zh: 我是他们的第一个 QA 招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'd never had QA before and they were like, we need to fix our things and we need automation.
zh: 他们以前从来没有过 QA，他们说，我们需要修复我们的东西，我们需要自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is kind of when CIs were up and coming.
zh: 那正是 CI 开始兴起的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: So kind of like 2006, because I've been in this industry for a while.
zh: 大概是 2006 年左右，因为我已经在这个行业待了一段时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, I started doing that.
zh: 是的，我开始做那份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then there was this weird thing called Selenium that was just starting out.
zh: 然后有一个叫 Selenium 的奇怪东西刚刚起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my wife is a musician, so she was away in the evenings with work.
zh: 我妻子是音乐家，所以她晚上要出去工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I started doing a lot of open source to support them because I was like, well, what else am I going to do in the evenings?
zh: 于是我开始做很多开源来支持他们，因为我想，晚上我还能干什么呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I wasn't that much of a gamer.
zh: 我不是那么爱玩游戏的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And started doing all of that, then got hired at Mozilla, spent a decade at Mozilla doing more open source, got into standards bodies, doing things like that, because as a whole, I kind of think the internet is this most amazing thing.
zh: 开始做这些之后，我受雇于 Mozilla，在 Mozilla 待了十年，做更多开源，进入标准机构，做这类事情，因为总的来说，我觉得互联网是最了不起的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's bad parts to it, but like with everything in life.
zh: 它有不好的一面，但生活中的万事万物都是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I really believed in Mozilla's mission.
zh: 我非常相信 Mozilla 的使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I spent a decade there.
zh: 所以我在那里待了十年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for the last six years, I've been working at BrowserStack.
zh: 然后在过去的六年里，我一直在 BrowserStack 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started up their open source program office, working with open source projects, supporting all of those, doing developer advocacy, supporting conferences, just trying to get the word out on what's the best way to develop software and test it.
zh: 我创办了他们的开源项目办公室，与开源项目合作，支持所有这些项目，做开发者布道，支持各类会议，只是努力宣传开发软件和测试软件的最佳方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go through that in order.
zh: 让我们按顺序过一遍这些经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were a QA at a shop that previously had not done very much of that.
zh: 你当时在一家以前没怎么做过 QA 的公司担任 QA。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is that experience like?
zh: 那是一段什么样的经历?

speaker: Unknown
en: How does that feel to you?
zh: 对你来说感觉如何?

speaker: Unknown
en: It was odd, especially because it was my first QA job as well.
zh: 挺奇怪的,尤其是因为那也是我的第一份 QA 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I had been working with a lot of QA people at the time when I was working at the bank.
zh: 因为我之前在银行工作时和很多 QA 人员打过交道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was interesting to kind of solve the problems.
zh: 去解决那些问题还挺有意思的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And nowadays, everything is so much easier because like, you know, from version control where you literally had to check the file out, no one else could work on the same file.
zh: 而如今,一切都容易太多了,因为,你知道,从版本控制说起——那时候你真的必须把文件签出,别人就无法在同一个文件上工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we were talking back in those days to...
zh: 比如我们那时候会讨论……

speaker: Unknown
en: How would a CI do things?
zh: CI 会怎么做这些事?

speaker: Unknown
en: How would you build out all of that?
zh: 你会怎么把这一切搭建起来?

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was interesting.
zh: 那很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I learned a lot.
zh: 我学到了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it helped my career a lot because I was given a lot of freedom.
zh: 而且我认为它对我的职业生涯帮助很大,因为我被给予了很大的自由。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I was just like, go figure it out for us because we don't have the time to figure it out.
zh: 然后他们就是那种:「去帮我们把它搞明白吧,因为我们没时间去弄清楚。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I had to be my own SRE in the QA environments.
zh: 所以我不得不在 QA 环境里当自己的 SRE。

speaker: Unknown
en: Had to build out automation frameworks around and help people do that.
zh: 必须搭建自动化框架,并帮助人们使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Introduced things like TDD because that was coming up through extreme programming at the time.
zh: 引入了像 TDD 这样的东西,因为那时候 TDD 正通过极限编程兴起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, wow, this is actually a really good idea.
zh: 我当时就想,哇,这真的是个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you're thinking about testing from the start.
zh: 就是你从一开始就在考虑测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we should do more of that.
zh: 我觉得我们应该更多地这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was fun.
zh: 那很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I spent, I think, four years at that company.
zh: 而且我想我在那家公司待了四年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like they're really great engineers, really great people to work with.
zh: 他们是非常优秀的工程师,非常好的共事者。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like marketing software.
zh: 那是做营销软件的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I also learned how to market myself because like I had to learn to be a marketer, to be a good QA, to understand their stuff.
zh: 所以我也学会了如何营销自己,因为我必须学会当一个营销人员,才能做好 QA、理解他们的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was, yeah, it was fun.
zh: 那是,嗯,那很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I was to go back in there, I'd probably change everything I did, but it was a great learning opportunity for me.
zh: 如果我回到那时候,我可能会改变我做过的每一件事,但对我来说那是一次很棒的学习机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is, just to quickly ask, what is one thing that comes top of mind that you would want to change from how you did things back in the day?
zh: 顺便快速问一句,回想你当年做事的方式,有没有一件最先浮现在脑海里、你想要改变的事?

speaker: Unknown
en: So the thing that probably stands out the most is I was trying to introduce, because DSLs were the fashion of the time, right?
zh: 最突出的大概是,我当时试图引入,因为 DSL 是那时候的时尚,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So you would take a framework and then build out using your language of choice, like how the API would be.
zh: 你会拿一个框架,然后用你选的语言去构建,比如 API 会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, oh, fluent APIs are really good.
zh: 我当时就想,哦,流式 API(fluent API)真的很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to build a DSL to our company.
zh: 所以我要为我们公司构建一个 DSL。

speaker: Unknown
en: So DSL for those listening is a domain-specific language, if you don't know what that means.
zh: 给不理解的听众解释一下,DSL 是领域特定语言(domain-specific language)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I built up this DSL, did it in a fluent way.
zh: 于是我构建了这个 DSL,用流式的方式来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was always like, do this dot, do that dot.
zh: 所以永远都是,做这个点(do this dot),做那个点(do that dot)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I built all of that and I was like, this is really cool.
zh: 我把这一切都建好了,我心想,这真的很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I started debugging it.
zh: 然后我开始调试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, wow, Fluent APIs are literally the worst, right?
zh: 我就想,哇,流式 API 简直是最糟糕的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because everything's a dot.
zh: 因为到处都是点。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you hit the debugger, you've got to go through so many layers just to get to where the real problem is.
zh: 当你打开调试器时,你得穿过那么多层才能找到真正的问题所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that would be my first thing.
zh: 所以那是我的第一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, don't do that.
zh: 就是,别那么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know it looks nice, but it's hard to work with.
zh: 我知道它看起来漂亮,但它很难用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do miss the days of jQuery and Fluent Everywhere and Linkback and C Sharp.
zh: 我确实怀念 jQuery、到处流式、以及 C Sharp 里 Linkback 的日子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those were fun, but agreed.
zh: 那些很有趣,但同意你的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But all right, let's move on to the next item.
zh: 好吧,我们进入下一项。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mozilla, you were there for, it sounds like, quite a while.
zh: Mozilla,听起来你在那里待了相当长的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it about the Mozilla mission that resonated with you?
zh: Mozilla 的使命中有什么引起了你的共鸣?

speaker: Unknown
en: So there were two parts to it.
zh: 有两个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I was at university, I got really into open source learning about what they were doing and the idea of that software should be free and if you want...
zh: 我上大学的时候,深深迷上了开源,去了解他们在做的事情,以及软件应该免费的理念,而如果你想要……

speaker: Unknown
en: services around that software, you pay for that, right?
zh: 围绕那个软件的服务,你就要为此付费,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But the idea is that you give out as much knowledge to the world to improve the world as a whole, right?
zh: 但这个想法是,你向世界分享尽可能多的知识,以改善整个世界,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that was always my belief in open source.
zh: 就像我一直对开源的信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Mozilla exuded that, right?
zh: 而 Mozilla 散发着这种气质,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And earlier, to me, the internet is the greatest invention that we have, right?
zh: 再早一点,对我来说,互联网是我们所拥有的最伟大的发明,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's this place where you can share knowledge, you can learn.
zh: 它是这样一个地方,你可以分享知识,可以学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ideally, it should be free for everyone to do that.
zh: 理想情况下,这应该对每个人都是免费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't necessarily always work out that way because capitalism doesn't work that way.
zh: 但它不一定总能如愿,因为资本主义不是那样运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's some really good things around it.
zh: 不过围绕它还是有一些非常好的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I was doing my interviews, the interview process when I joined, so when I joined, there was 350 people at Missilla, like really, really small company.
zh: 我在面试的时候,也就是我加入时的面试流程,当时 Missilla 只有 350 人,真的是非常小的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But everyone I met was probably the smartest person I'd ever met on the planet, right?
zh: 但我遇到的每个人都可能是我这辈子在地球上遇到过的最聪明的人,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like they were just these people who were like, we've got to solve these really hard problems and at scale and make the world a better place, right?
zh: 他们就是这样的人:我们必须解决这些非常难的问题,而且是规模化地解决,让世界变得更美好,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that was their belief.
zh: 那就是他们的信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, okay, this is really a place for me.
zh: 我就想,好吧,这里真的是属于我的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're all super nice people all from around the world.
zh: 而且他们都是非常友善的人,来自世界各地。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was looking to change jobs because I was driving like an hour to work to Southampton and my wife was pregnant at the time.
zh: 我当时正想换工作,因为我每天要开车大约一小时去 Southampton 上班,而我妻子那时正怀着孕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, you know, I don't want to be driving like an hour there and an hour back because I'm aside on family time.
zh: 我就想,你知道,我不想来回各开一小时车,因为这挤占了我的家庭时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then by accident, I found Mozilla were hiring, went through the process and I was like, okay, this is a really cool place to go work at because the technology, the people, kind of you talking about jQuery, like when I was there, the creator of jQuery was working at Mozilla at the same time, met Brendan Eich, the creator of JavaScript.
zh: 后来机缘巧合,我发现 Mozilla 在招人,走了一遍流程,我想,好吧,这真是个很酷的工作地方,因为技术、人,就像你提到 jQuery,我在那的时候,jQuery 的创造者也在 Mozilla 工作,还见到了 JavaScript 的创造者 Brendan Eich。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was like, there's these super smart people who are willing to tell you everything and share their knowledge.
zh: 所以就是,有这些超级聪明的人,愿意告诉你一切、分享他们的知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I learned so much every day that I worked there.
zh: 我在那工作的每一天都学到很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sounds like a lovely place.
zh: 听起来是个很棒的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: What were you working on when you started?
zh: 你刚入职时在做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: When I joined, I joined as a QA lead on a project called Socorro, which is the website that allows people to see when Firefox crashes, why it was crashing.
zh: 我加入时,是作为一个叫 Socorro 的项目的 QA 负责人,这个网站让人们可以看到 Firefox 崩溃时,是什么原因导致崩溃的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you could see stack traces, things like that.
zh: 所以你可以看到堆栈追踪之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the interesting thing is when you got, well, I think at the time there was over 500 million users.
zh: 有意思的是,当时,我记得那时用户数超过 5 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: When there's a crash, even if it's a 1% crash on 500 million, that's a lot of data coming in.
zh: 一旦有崩溃,哪怕 5 亿用户里只有 1% 的崩溃率,那也是海量的数据涌进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was like a lot of learning how to scale, things like that, putting us through its paces.
zh: 所以就是大量学习如何扩展之类的东西,让我们经受了一番历练。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I did that for maybe four or five months.
zh: 这样做了大概四五个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I got moved into a team called the Automation and Tools Team, which built a lot of the testing frameworks.
zh: 然后我被调进一个叫自动化与工具团队(Automation and Tools Team)的团队,他们构建了很多测试框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: That Mozilla used because everything had to be handcrafted.
zh: 是 Mozilla 用的,因为一切都得手工打造。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you can't just go buy a tool off the internet type thing and it'll work.

zh: 我被雇的时候，我受雇要做的事情之一，就是回馈那些造就了 BrowserStack 的社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was like, David, go work on Selenium still, right?
zh: 就是那种「David，你去继续做 Selenium 吧」。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's what we want to do because it's important to us as a company to maintain good relations with that.
zh: 就是我们想做这个，因为和那个社区保持良好关系对我们公司来说很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: We definitely don't want to own any of the Selenium stuff.
zh: 我们绝对不想占有 Selenium 的任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to be able to keep there.
zh: 我们想留在那个生态里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same with Appium.
zh: Appium 也一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have a very good relationship with the Appium folks, WebDriver.io, do all of that.
zh: 所以我和 Appium 的人、WebDriver.io 关系都很好，这些都在做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I still get to maintain a lot of the work that I do through standards.
zh: 而且我仍然可以通过标准来维护我所做的大量工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which of course our competitors benefit from, but everyone benefits.
zh: 这当然让我们的竞争对手也受益，但所有人都受益。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the idea is hopefully a rising tide lifts all ships, right?
zh: 理念就是，希望水涨船高，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And makes everyone's life easier along the way.
zh: 并且在这一路上让每个人的生活都更轻松。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do a lot of that and then go to conferences and like, hey, here's this really cool thing that we've built out, or we're doing this thing and we're giving it away because it's important to the industry and things like that.
zh: 所以我做了很多这类工作，然后去各种大会，讲「嘿，我们做了这个很酷的东西」，或者「我们在做这个，而且我们会把它免费送出去，因为它对整个行业很重要」之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You reference the difficulties of joining the utopia that is open source with the real world that is capitalism.
zh: 你刚才提到了加入开源这个乌托邦与资本主义这个现实世界之间的困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's say that I'm a big company executive and I work on tooling and such that interacts with open source.
zh: 那假设我是一个大公司的高管，我做的是与开源交互的工具之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: How would you try to convince me that we should have someone like you who tries to lift all boats with the rising tide, including our competitors?
zh: 你会怎么说服我，让我们应该雇一个像你这样的人，去试图用水涨船高的方式把所有的船都抬起来，包括我们的竞争对手？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the simplest one to an executive, because executives think of everything within risks, right?
zh: 我觉得对高管来说最简单的说法是，因为高管看一切都是从风险出发的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the risk of everyone stopping work on their projects?
zh: 所有人都停止为他们那些项目做贡献的风险是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's the biggest one, right?
zh: 我觉得这是最大的风险，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've seen through various open source engineers who've got to the end of their tether and just gone, you know what?
zh: 我们见过各种开源工程师走到忍无可忍的地步,直接说:你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to hell.
zh: 见鬼去吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they poisoned their whole project, which then poisoned everything.
zh: 然后他们把整个项目都下了毒，这又毒害了一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was one that happened, I think, kind of 2020, like just during the pandemic.
zh: 有一个事件，我记得大概是 2020 年，就在疫情期间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was Leftshift, which was a node package.
zh: 我记得是 Leftshift，一个 node 包。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the engineer had been asking people like, hey, I've lost my job.
zh: 那个工程师一直在请求大家，嘿，我失业了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll rely on me for this thing.
zh: 你们都依赖我这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could I have some money, please?
zh: 能不能给我一点钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: And no one gave him money.
zh: 而没有人给他钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he poisoned all these packages and then deleted all the code.
zh: 然后他给所有这些包下了毒，然后把代码全删了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's the big thing.
zh: 我觉得这就是最大的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the worst case.
zh: 这是最坏的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: The real reason why I think a lot of companies should do it is I'm sure a lot of people got taught about it during school, but like corporate responsibility is actually a big thing.
zh: 而我认为很多公司应该这么做的真正原因是，我敢肯定很多人在学校里学过，企业责任其实是一件很重要的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to look after the things that make you money.
zh: 你需要照看好那些让你赚钱的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a whole, right?
zh: 整体而言，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Supplies and things like that.
zh: 供应链之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And especially in the age of AI, I think supply chain attacks are going to become a lot more prevalent.
zh: 尤其是在 AI 时代，我认为供应链攻击会变得更加普遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're in there and helping secure everything, yes, you give away some things, but at the end of the day, you're making sure your business is as risk-free as possible.
zh: 所以如果你参与进去帮忙保障一切的安全，是的，你会送出去一些东西，但说到底，你是在确保你的业务尽可能没有风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's never going to be zero risk, but as risk-free as possible.
zh: 风险永远不会是零，但要尽可能没有风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would imagine having someone like you who's deeply familiar with the spec and also the politics and people behind it is probably quite useful for the company too.
zh: 我可以想象，雇一个像你这样对规范本身、以及规范背后的政治和人脉都深谙于心的人，对公司来说应该也很有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, if there's a feature you want to work or like to make sure some area is better kept.
zh: 你知道，如果有一个你想推进的特性，或者想确保某个领域被维护得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, definitely.
zh: 对，对，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other side of it is that if there's major problems that as a, say our website and our product is having with say Google Chrome, I have enough contacts that I can just reach out to folks at Google Chrome and go, hey, we've got this bug, could you help us?
zh: 另一方面是，如果出现了重大问题——比如说我们的网站和我们的产品在使用 Google Chrome 时有问题——我有足够的人脉，可以直接联系 Google Chrome 的人说，嘿，我们遇到这个 bug 了，你们能帮帮我们吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've reproduced it.
zh: 而且我们已经复现了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here we go.
zh: 给，就是这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you prioritize it for us?
zh: 能不能为我们优先处理一下？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a lot of give and take that then becomes really good.
zh: 所以这里面有很多你来我往，而且回报非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then again, it's us giving to Chrome and going, hey, your product's got this bug.
zh: 然后同样，也是我们向 Chrome 反馈说，嘿，你们的产品有这个 bug。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's get rid of it.
zh: 咱们把它解决掉吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It benefits us, but it also benefits other people.
zh: 这对我们有好处，但对其他人也有好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure the Chrome people like that, yeah.
zh: 我敢肯定 Chrome 那边的人会喜欢这个的，是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly, right?
zh: 完全正确，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Every engineer doesn't want to be writing code that's full of bugs, right?
zh: 没有哪个工程师愿意写满是 bug 的代码，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And bugs are always something that's not tested.
zh: 而 bug 永远是那些没被测试到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, the bug's always there, right?
zh: 就是说，bug 一直都在那儿，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's never been tested in that way.
zh: 只是从来没有被那样测试过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, oh, by the way, now I can go fix it.
zh: 然后就变成，哦，对了，现在我可以去修它了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of fixing and detecting bugs, let's talk about another role play.
zh: 说到修复和检测 bug，我们再来聊聊另一个角色扮演。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am a website or company that has a website.
zh: 我是一个网站，或者说是一家有网站的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would I care about BrowserStack or any of the other things we're talking about?
zh: 我为什么要关心 BrowserStack 或者我们正在谈论的其他这些东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think part of it, so if you've got a website, how much do you care if people actually use it?
zh: 我觉得其中一部分是，如果你有一个网站，你有多在乎人们是否真的在使用它？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't care that people use your website, then like browser stack's not going to be any use to you, right?
zh: 如果你不在乎人们是否使用你的网站，那么 BrowserStack 对你来说就没什么用，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I think that's the, like if it's just a marketing front page, who cares?
zh: 就是说，如果它只是一个营销首页，谁在乎呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have a software as a service company, I think it tends to be really important that you at least have one test for every critical path.
zh: 如果你有一家软件即服务(SaaS)公司，我觉得至少为每一条关键路径都有一个测试，这一点往往非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's the most important way.
zh: 我认为这是最重要的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't mean you need browser stack, but every critical path, once you start writing one test for every critical path becomes important and it becomes bigger and bigger and bigger.
zh: 这不意味着你需要 BrowserStack，但每一条关键路径，一旦你开始为每条关键路径写一个测试，它就变得重要起来，而且会变得越来越大、越来越大、越来越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's regulatory things that also need to be put in there.
zh: 然后还有监管方面的事情也需要放进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Biggest one that's been on people's minds for years is accessibility, right?
zh: 多年来人们最关心的一点就是无障碍访问，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's going to be really big.
zh: 我认为这会变得非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the AI space, I think governance is going to be another big one that I think a lot of people are going to need to care about and how that interacts with everything.
zh: 在 AI 领域，我认为治理会是另一个很重要的事情，我想很多人都会需要关心它，以及它如何与所有东西交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of people just see the price and they don't look at how much am I, from a cognitive load, am I taking off from the company, right?
zh: 所以很多人只看价格，却不去看我从公司身上卸下了多少认知负担，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So even if I didn't work at BrowserStack, I would always recommend people use a BrowserStack-like company.
zh: 所以即使我不是在 BrowserStack 工作，我也会一直推荐人们使用一家类 BrowserStack 的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where possible, because if you're gonna hire people to maintain infrastructure for that, you can't just hire one person, has to be two people, right?
zh: 在可能的情况下，因为如果你要雇人维护那套基础设施，你不能只雇一个人，得雇两个人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you need to have a backup because otherwise the bus factor is really bad.
zh: 因为你需要有备份，否则巴士系数就非常糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it's the, how much maintenance do they do constantly?
zh: 然后就是，他们要持续做多少维护？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you've got all this other infrastructure where a lot of these companies like BrowserStack
zh: 然后你还有这一大堆其他的基础设施，而像 BrowserStack 这样的很多公司

speaker: Unknown
en: We're able to spread the costs around a little bit easier.
zh: 能够更容易地把成本摊薄一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we take a lot of that heavy lifting and then people don't need to care about it.
zh: 我们承担了其中大量的繁重工作，然后人们就不需要关心这些了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just know that it works and you've got SLAs and you've got all of that.
zh: 他们只知道它能正常工作，而且你有 SLA，你有所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then life's a lot easier that way if you don't have that cognitive load on you when you can just think, I need to test this.
zh: 这样一来，如果你身上没有那种认知负担，生活就会轻松很多，你只需要想，我需要测试这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to make sure my product is high quality.
zh: 我需要确保我的产品质量高。

speaker: Unknown
en: High quality products lead to more sales for me.
zh: 高质量的产品会给我带来更多销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's very convincing.
zh: 这非常有说服力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd like to go through each of the three main areas you touched on and ask for some advice here, because I think a lot of our listeners are perhaps getting started or have existing flows, perhaps even through browser stack, but it can be hard to know what should I test?
zh: 我想逐一过一遍你提到的三个主要领域，并就每项请教一些建议，因为我想我们的很多听众可能正在起步，或者已经有一些现有流程，甚至可能已经在通过 BrowserStack 使用了，但很难知道我该测试什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How should I test it?
zh: 我该怎么测试它？

speaker: Unknown
en: So do you have any tips or algorithms for I have a SaaS or I have an existing complex website?
zh: 那么你有没有什么技巧或算法，针对“我有一个 SaaS，或者我有一个现有的复杂网站”这种情况？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I know what I should test to begin with?
zh: 一开始我怎么知道我该测试什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the advice I always give, and I've kind of alluded to it already, is the create one test and build up from there.
zh: 我一直给的建议，我已经有点提到过了，就是先创建一个测试，然后从那里逐步扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ideally you should only have one test for one critical path, because if you have thoughts about how you're architecting your system, you'll have other layers of protections built in from observability to telemetry to kind of everything in between, right?
zh: 理想情况下，每条关键路径应该只有一个测试，因为如果你对如何架构你的系统有过思考，你就会有其他层面的保护措施内置其中，从可观测性到遥测，以及介于两者之间的一切，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see, and logging, you can see all these things.
zh: 然后你就能看到，还有日志，你可以看到所有这些东西

speaker: Unknown
en: happening in real time.
zh: 实时发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you have that one test that I can log in and do X and that's solved, that's great.
zh: 但如果你有那一个测试——我能登录并完成 X——那个问题解决了，那就很棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you try to work out which of those different layers become a lot more important along the way.
zh: 然后你试着弄清楚这些不同的层级中哪些在此过程中变得更加重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that when you go, oh, I need to add another test.
zh: 这样当你说，哦，我需要再加一个测试时，

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, well, this is a critical path test.
zh: 就像，好吧，这是一个关键路径测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to do this rather than I've got 15 tests that are roughly doing the same thing.
zh: 我需要做这个，而不是我有 15 个大致在做同样事情的测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each test is going to take like a minute.
zh: 每个测试大概要花一分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's 15 minutes of testing.
zh: 那就是15分钟的测试时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you really need to wait 15 minutes?
zh: 你真的需要等15分钟吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's about trying to balance how long things take, how critical, and then what is the risk factor within that?
zh: 所以这是在试着平衡事情花费多长时间、有多关键，以及其中的风险因素是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There is no one way, but it's about balancing all of those along the way so that you get the best out of it.
zh: 没有唯一的方法，但在过程中平衡所有这些因素，这样你才能从中获得最大的收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like if your test suite takes 24 hours to run, could you start splitting that into multiple runs throughout the day, but it's in different sections or things like that?
zh: 就像如果你的测试套件需要24小时才能运行完，你能不能把它拆分成一天中多次运行，分成不同的部分之类的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then suddenly, the more you do in parallel, the quicker you get.
zh: 然后突然之间，你并行做的越多，速度就越快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then again, coming back to the cognitive load, you don't have to go, oh, what was I doing again 24 hours ago before I found that bug?
zh: 再回到认知负荷这一点，你不必说，哦，在我发现那个 bug 之前24小时我在做什么来着？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And trying to do that.
zh: 并试着那样去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like speed versus correctness versus risk.
zh: 所以这就是速度 vs 正确性 vs 风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting.
zh: 这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people refer to things like having smaller test suites or more rapid development cycles in reference to unit testing or even integration testing.
zh: 很多人提到更小的测试套件或更快的开发周期，都是在说单元测试甚至集成测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're using very similar terminology here for the end-to-end browser testing to try to make it easier for developers to use.
zh: 而你在这里用非常相似的术语来形容端到端浏览器测试，试图让它对开发者来说更容易使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I've seen in my career is a lot of people tend to do lots of unit tests, like do the pyramid, right?
zh: 我在职业生涯中看到的是很多人倾向于写大量单元测试，就是做那个金字塔，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Testing pyramid.
zh: 测试金字塔。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have small tests at the bottom, medium tests in the middle, and long tests at the top.
zh: 底部是小测试，中间是中等测试，顶部是长测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously it should shrink from bottom to top.
zh: 显然它应该从底部到顶部逐渐缩小。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've also seen a lot of people move to a space, especially now that component testing is a thing around like React and Vue and all of that.
zh: 我也见过很多人转向另一个空间，尤其是现在组件测试成为了一件事，围绕 React、Vue 之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like how do you test this one component?
zh: 比如你怎么测试这一个组件？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they build out either a Christmas tree shape in their testing pyramid or I've seen someone else describe it as the testing hourglass.
zh: 然后他们把测试金字塔建成圣诞树形状，或者我见过别人把它描述为测试沙漏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where it kind of shrinks above and then shoots out again very quickly.
zh: 就是它先向上收缩，然后又很快地向外扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want that, which is why I think writing one test is the most important for each critical path.
zh: 你不想要那样，这就是为什么我认为为每条关键路径只写一个测试是最重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because then you've got that really good one test for doing your thing, that really good one test for accessibility, one test for visual testing, one test for everything else.
zh: 因为那样你就有了一个真正好的测试来做你的事情，一个真正好的测试做无障碍测试，一个测试做视觉测试，一个测试做其他所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And suddenly you might have a hundred tests.
zh: 突然之间你可能有了100个测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: But those 100 tests are the most important tests you need when you've got a browser, because browsers starting up are really expensive in compute time, right?
zh: 但这100个测试是你有浏览器时需要的最重要的测试，因为启动浏览器在计算时间上非常昂贵，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you want it to be as fast as possible, but browsers are so complex, they're effectively operating systems in themselves nowadays, right?
zh: 你想让它尽可能快，但浏览器太复杂了，如今它们本身实际上就是操作系统，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have Chrome OS, we used to have Firefox OS, right?
zh: 我们有 Chrome OS，我们曾经有过 Firefox OS，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, they're incredibly complex.
zh: 就像，它们复杂得难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're constantly starting them up,
zh: 所以如果你不断地启动它们，

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just booting a computer each time, and it's a computer within a computer.
zh: 你每次都相当于在启动一台电脑，而且是一台电脑里再套一台电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's see if you can shrink things down and think about where you're testing it at a better place.
zh: 所以让我们看看你能不能把规模缩小下来，思考在一个更好的地方进行测试。

en: Do you think that as people get more familiar with AI, these problems will become lesser?

speaker: Unknown
en: When I was working on browsers, one of the things that was always driven into us was always think about these lists of problems that come up.
zh: 我以前做浏览器的时候，一直被灌输的事情之一就是要始终考虑这些会出现的各类问题。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 其中很多是你我从构建软件中获得的知识经验。

zh: 但如果人们从未构建过软件、从未从一开始就被反复灌输这些，我觉得那真的很危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think while I like AI, I kind of feel like junior engineers should be using it a lot less, more of a backup to review their stuff and go, hey, did you think about this problem, that problem, right?
zh: 我虽然喜欢 AI，但我觉得初级工程师应该少用它，把它更多当作一个备份来审查他们的东西，问一句，嘿，你有没有考虑过这个那个问题，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Mostly so that they can have that knowledge drummed into them from the start.

speaker: Unknown
en: But then go do what you need.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: But then it needs to be rewritten or at least go through security checks to make sure that if the prototype goes to production, it's safe.
zh: 但之后它需要被重写，或者至少要经过安全检查，以确保如果原型进入生产环境，它是安全的。

speaker: Unknown

en: AI will hallucinate.

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an interesting one.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's see if I can replicate it, how it came in.
zh: 让我看看能不能复现它是怎么进来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you can try figure out how that person was doing it rather than going, I don't know how to start this.
zh: 现在你就可以试着弄清楚那个人是怎么做的，而不是说，我不知道该怎么开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me figure it out.
zh: 让我想想办法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then kind of spending time.
